title: Practice: scales and bearings
intro: Eleven questions. Answers you would get from a careful scale drawing are accepted — you do not need to be exact to the kilometre.

questions.prompt: Quick-fire: write each direction as a three-figure bearing, e.g. 045.
questions.explanation: Bearings are measured clockwise from North. A back bearing is the original bearing $\pm 180^\circ$.

questions.prompt: Set the pointer to a bearing of $147^\circ$. Then read off roughly how far East and South a 100 km journey on that bearing goes.
hints: $147^\circ$ is between East ($090^\circ$) and South ($180^\circ$), a bit closer to South.
questions.explanation: At $147^\circ$ the journey goes about 54 km East and 84 km South — the same as the scale drawing in the lesson.

questions.prompt: Which of these is written correctly as a bearing?
questions.explanation: Bearings are always written with three figures, so $47^\circ$ becomes $047^\circ$. They are never negative — they run from $000^\circ$ to $359^\circ$.

questions.prompt: B is on a bearing of $070^\circ$ from A. What is the bearing of A from B?
hints: Turn round to face the other way: add $180^\circ$.

questions.prompt: Ship A is on a bearing of $280^\circ$ from ship B. Set the pointer to the bearing of **B from A**.
questions.explanation: $280^\circ - 180^\circ = 100^\circ$. A is roughly West of B, so B is roughly East of A — and $100^\circ$ is just South of East.

questions.prompt: A map has a scale of $1 : 100\,000$. Two parks are 3.6 cm apart on the map. How far apart are they in real life, in **metres**?
hints: 1 cm on the map is $100\,000$ cm $= 1000$ m in real life.

questions.prompt: On a map drawn at 1 cm to 20 km, how long should you draw a journey of 150 km?
A ship sails 100 km on each bearing. Use the bearing explorer or a scale drawing to fill in the distances, to the nearest km.
hints: As the bearing gets closer to $180^\circ$, the ship goes further South and less far East.
Draw each journey as 5 cm at 1 cm to 20 km, then measure.
questions.explanation: $132^\circ$: 74 km E, 67 km S. $151^\circ$: 48 km E, 87 km S. $165^\circ$: 26 km E, 97 km S. Answers within 2 km are fine for a scale drawing.

questions.prompt: Work backwards from the finishing point.
questions.scenario: After sailing from port P, a ship finishes 10 km East and 20 km South of its starting point.

steps.prompt: Roughly which direction did it sail?
steps.feedback: It went further South (20 km) than East (10 km).

steps.prompt: From a scale drawing, what is the bearing of the journey, to the nearest degree?
steps.hint: The line is $27^\circ$ East of due South. Due South is $180^\circ$.

steps.prompt: How far did it sail, to the nearest km?
steps.hint: Measure the long side, or use Pythagoras: $\sqrt{10^2 + 20^2}$.

questions.explanation: The journey is $27^\circ$ East of South, so its bearing is $180^\circ - 27^\circ = 153^\circ$, and the distance is $\sqrt{10^2 + 20^2} \approx 22$ km.

questions.prompt: A ship sails on a bearing of $236^\circ$. Select **every** true statement.
questions.explanation: $236^\circ$ lies between South ($180^\circ$) and West ($270^\circ$), so the ship goes both South and West.

questions.prompt: Ship A is 36 km from ship B. How far apart are they on a map with a scale of $1 : 400\,000$?
hints: 1 cm on this map is 4 km.
questions.explanation: $400\,000$ cm $= 4$ km, so 1 cm represents 4 km. $36 \div 4 = 9$ cm.
